questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes booting?

options.A: The process of starting or restarting a computer and loading the operating system into memory so that the system becomes ready for use
options.B: The process of installing application software
options.C: The process of deleting files from the hard disk
options.D: The process of connecting a computer to a network

questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting or restarting a computer and loading the operating system into memory so that the system becomes ready for use.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes speed as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.B: The ability to perform very large numbers of operations in a short time
options.C: The ability to repeat tasks without getting tired
options.D: The ability to use many different kinds of tasks

questions.explanation: A computer can perform very large numbers of operations in a short time. Processing speed is commonly expressed using units such as hertz (Hz) and its multiples.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes accuracy as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to perform very large numbers of operations in a short time
options.B: The ability to produce highly accurate results when the input data, instructions and hardware are correct
options.C: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.D: The ability to repeat tasks without getting tired

questions.explanation: A computer can produce highly accurate results when the input data, instructions and hardware are correct; incorrect input or instructions can produce incorrect output.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes diligence as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to produce accurate results
options.B: The ability to repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired or losing concentration in the human sense
options.C: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.D: The ability to perform many different kinds of tasks

questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired or losing concentration in the human sense.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes storage capacity as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to perform very large numbers of operations in a short time
options.B: The ability to store large quantities of data and retrieve them when required
options.C: The ability to repeat tasks without getting tired
options.D: The ability to produce the same result repeatedly

questions.explanation: A computer can store large quantities of data and retrieve them when required, using primary memory and secondary storage devices.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes automation as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.B: The ability to carry out specified operations automatically with limited human intervention once a program and required data are supplied
options.C: The ability to perform many different kinds of tasks
options.D: The ability to produce accurate results

questions.explanation: Automation means that, once a program and required data are supplied, a computer can carry out the specified operations automatically with limited human intervention.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes multitasking?

options.A: The ability of a computer to store large quantities of data
options.B: The operating system's ability to manage more than one task or program during the same period by sharing processor time and other resources
options.C: The ability of a computer to perform calculations automatically
options.D: The ability of a computer to produce the same result repeatedly

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the operating system's ability to manage more than one task or program during the same period, by sharing processor time and other resources.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in banking and finance?

options.A: Only for printing passbooks
options.B: For account management, electronic fund transfers, ATM services, online banking, transaction processing, financial analysis, accounting and fraud monitoring
options.C: Only for customer relationship management

questions.explanation: Computers support account management, electronic fund transfers, ATM services, online banking, transaction processing, financial analysis, accounting and fraud monitoring.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in industry and manufacturing?

options.A: Only for production planning
options.B: For automation, robotics, computer-aided design (CAD), computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), quality control, process monitoring and production planning
options.C: Only for quality control

questions.explanation: They support automation, robotics, computer-aided design (CAD), computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), quality control, process monitoring and production planning.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in defence and security?

options.A: Only for communication
options.B: For communication, surveillance systems, training simulations, logistics, intelligence analysis, navigation and command-and-control systems, subject to strict security controls
options.C: Only for training simulations

questions.explanation: They support communication, surveillance systems, training simulations, logistics, intelligence analysis, navigation and command-and-control systems, subject to strict security controls.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in agriculture?

options.A: Only for weather information
options.B: For weather and market information, precision farming, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation control, farm management and analysis of satellite or sensor data
options.C: Only for irrigation control

questions.explanation: They support weather and market information, precision farming, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation control, farm management and analysis of satellite or sensor data.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in entertainment and media?

options.A: Only for gaming
options.B: For gaming, animation, video and audio editing, digital photography, streaming, publishing and special effects
options.C: Only for video and audio editing

questions.explanation: They are used for gaming, animation, video and audio editing, digital photography, streaming, publishing and special effects.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in transportation?

options.A: Only for ticket reservations
options.B: For ticket reservations, traffic management, navigation, vehicle control systems, logistics, scheduling and tracking of goods
options.C: Only for navigation

questions.explanation: They support ticket reservations, traffic management, navigation, vehicle control systems, logistics, scheduling and tracking of goods.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in communication?

options.A: Only for email
options.B: For email, instant messaging, video conferencing, internet-based voice calls, social networking and sharing of digital files
options.C: Only for video conferencing

questions.explanation: They enable email, instant messaging, video conferencing, internet-based voice calls, social networking and sharing of digital files.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in science and research?

options.A: Only for sharing research results
options.B: For data analysis, modelling, simulation, scientific calculations, managing experiments, processing observations and sharing research results
options.C: Only for scientific calculations

questions.explanation: They are used for data analysis, modelling, simulation, scientific calculations, managing experiments, processing observations and sharing research results.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in hospitals and healthcare?

options.A: Only for billing patients
options.B: For electronic health records, appointment systems, diagnostic imaging, laboratory information systems, hospital administration, telemedicine and medical research
options.C: Only for medical research

questions.explanation: They support electronic health records, appointment systems, diagnostic imaging, laboratory information systems, hospital administration, telemedicine and medical research.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in education?

options.A: Only for playing games
options.B: For online learning, digital classrooms, examinations, educational content, research, simulations, student records and preparation of teaching materials
options.C: Only for maintaining accounts

questions.explanation: Computers support online learning, digital classrooms, examinations, educational content, research, simulations, student records and preparation of teaching materials.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in business and commerce?

options.A: Only for communication
options.B: For billing, inventory control, payroll, accounting, customer relationship management, e-commerce, data analysis, communication and preparation of business reports
options.C: Only for payroll

questions.explanation: They are used for billing, inventory control, payroll, accounting, customer relationship management, e-commerce, data analysis, communication and preparation of business reports.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in government administration?

options.A: Only for preparing official reports
options.B: For e-governance, maintaining public records, processing applications, delivering online services, managing revenue and preparing official reports
options.C: Only for managing revenue

questions.explanation: Government offices use computers for e-governance, maintaining public records, processing applications, delivering online services, managing revenue and preparing official reports.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the classification of computers according to the type of data they process?

options.A: Microcomputers, minicomputers, mainframes and supercomputers
options.B: Analog computers, digital computers and hybrid computers
options.C: General-purpose and special-purpose computers

questions.explanation: According to the type of data they process, computers are commonly classified as analog computers, digital computers and hybrid computers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes an analog computer?

options.A: A computer that processes data in discrete binary form
options.B: A computer that represents and processes continuously varying physical quantities such as temperature, pressure, speed or voltage
options.C: A computer that combines analog and digital methods
options.D: A computer designed for individual use

questions.explanation: An analog computer represents and processes continuously varying physical quantities, such as temperature, pressure, speed or voltage.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a digital computer?

options.A: A computer that processes continuously varying physical quantities
options.B: A computer that processes data in discrete form, usually using binary digits (0 and 1)
options.C: A computer that combines analog and digital methods
options.D: A computer designed only for scientific simulation

questions.explanation: A digital computer processes data in discrete form, usually using binary digits (0 and 1). Most modern personal computers, smartphones and servers are digital computers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a hybrid computer?

options.A: A computer that only processes continuous physical values
options.B: A computer that combines analog measurement or processing with digital computation, often converting signals between analog and digital forms
options.C: A computer that only processes binary data
options.D: A computer designed for individual use only

questions.explanation: A hybrid computer combines analog measurement or processing with digital computation, often converting signals between analog and digital forms. It is used in specialised monitoring, simulation and control applications.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a microcomputer?

options.A: A computer based on a microprocessor and designed primarily for individual use
options.B: A computer designed for large-scale transaction processing
options.C: A computer designed for the highest computational performance

questions.explanation: A microcomputer is a computer based on a microprocessor and designed primarily for individual use. Desktop PCs, laptops and many single-board computers are examples.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a personal computer (PC)?

options.A: A computer designed for use by one person at a time, although it may be connected to shared networks and services
options.B: A computer designed for many concurrent users only
options.C: A computer designed for the highest computational performance
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A personal computer is a general-purpose computer designed for use by one person at a time, although it may be connected to shared networks and services.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a desktop computer?

options.A: A portable computer with an integrated screen and battery
options.B: A personal computer designed to be used at a fixed location, typically with a separate monitor, keyboard and pointing device
options.C: A computer operated mainly through a touchscreen
options.D: A high-performance computer for professional technical tasks

questions.explanation: A desktop computer is a personal computer designed to be used at a fixed location, typically with a separate monitor, keyboard and pointing device.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a laptop computer?

options.A: A portable personal computer with an integrated screen, keyboard, pointing device, battery and computing components
options.B: A computer designed to be used at a fixed location
options.C: A computer operated mainly through a touchscreen
options.D: A high-performance computer for engineering design

questions.explanation: A laptop is a portable personal computer with an integrated screen, keyboard, pointing device, battery and computing components.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a tablet computer?

options.A: A computer designed for large-scale transaction processing
options.B: A portable computer usually operated mainly through a touchscreen, with an on-screen or optional physical keyboard
options.C: A high-performance computer for scientific work
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A tablet is a portable computer, usually operated mainly through a touchscreen, with an on-screen or optional physical keyboard.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a workstation?

options.A: A portable computer with an integrated battery
options.B: A high-performance computer intended for professional technical tasks such as engineering design, scientific work, 3D graphics and specialised data processing
options.C: A computer designed for very large-scale transaction processing
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A workstation is a high-performance computer intended for professional technical tasks such as engineering design, scientific work, 3D graphics and specialised data processing.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a minicomputer?

options.A: A historical midrange multi-user computer category, generally smaller than a mainframe but more capable than many early microcomputers
options.B: A computer designed for the highest computational performance
options.C: A portable computer operated through a touchscreen
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A minicomputer is a historical midrange multi-user computer category, generally smaller than a mainframe but more capable than many early microcomputers. The term is now largely obsolete.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a mainframe computer?

options.A: A portable computer with an integrated battery
options.B: A powerful, highly reliable system designed to handle large volumes of transactions, data and concurrent users, commonly used by banks, governments and large organisations
options.C: A computer designed for individual use only
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A mainframe is a powerful, highly reliable system designed to handle large volumes of transactions, data and concurrent users, commonly used by banks, governments and large organisations.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a supercomputer?

options.A: A computer designed for individual use
options.B: An extremely high-performance computer designed for computationally intensive tasks such as climate modelling, scientific simulation, complex physics and large-scale research
options.C: A computer designed for large-scale transaction processing

questions.explanation: A supercomputer is an extremely high-performance computer designed for computationally intensive tasks such as climate modelling, scientific simulation, complex physics and large-scale research.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a server?

options.A: A computer or software system that provides services, data or resources to other computers (clients) over a network
options.B: A computer designed for the highest computational performance
options.C: A portable computer operated through a touchscreen
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A server is a computer or software system that provides services, data or resources to other computers (clients) over a network.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes an embedded computer?

options.A: A high-performance computer for scientific simulation
options.B: A computing system built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions, such as in vehicles, appliances, medical equipment and industrial machines
options.C: A portable computer operated through a touchscreen
options.D: A computer designed for large-scale transaction processing

questions.explanation: An embedded computer is a computing system built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions, such as in vehicles, appliances, medical equipment and industrial machines.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a mobile computer?

options.A: A computer designed to be used at a fixed location
options.B: A portable computing device such as a laptop, tablet or smartphone, designed to be used while being carried or moved
options.C: A computing system built into a larger device
options.D: A computer designed for the highest computational performance

questions.explanation: A mobile computer is a portable computing device, such as a laptop, tablet or smartphone, designed to be used while being carried or moved.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a wearable computer?

options.A: A computer designed to be worn on the body, such as a smartwatch or certain health-monitoring devices
options.B: A computer built into a vehicle
options.C: A computer designed for large-scale transaction processing
options.D: A high-performance computer for engineering design

questions.explanation: A wearable computer is a computing device designed to be worn on the body, such as a smartwatch or certain health-monitoring devices.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a single-board computer?

options.A: A computer designed for large-scale transaction processing
options.B: A complete computer built on one circuit board, with processor, memory and input/output interfaces; often used for education, prototyping and embedded projects
options.C: A portable computer operated through a touchscreen
options.D: A computer designed for the highest computational performance

questions.explanation: A single-board computer is a complete computer built on one circuit board, with processor, memory and input/output interfaces; it is often used for education, prototyping and embedded projects.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a general-purpose computer?

options.A: A computer designed to perform only one specific task
options.B: A computer that can run many different programs and perform a wide variety of tasks such as document preparation, calculations, browsing and data analysis
options.C: A computer designed for the highest computational performance
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A general-purpose computer can run many different programs and perform a wide variety of tasks, such as document preparation, calculations, browsing and data analysis.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a special-purpose computer?

options.A: A computer designed or configured to perform a specific task or a limited set of tasks, such as controlling a traffic signal or operating a dedicated industrial system
options.B: A computer that can run many different programs
options.C: A computer designed for the highest computational performance
options.D: A portable computer operated through a touchscreen

questions.explanation: A special-purpose computer is designed or configured to perform a specific task or a limited set of tasks, such as controlling a traffic signal or operating a dedicated industrial system.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the first generation of computers?

options.A: They used vacuum tubes, magnetic drums or other early storage, punched cards and paper tape; they were relatively slow, required substantial space and maintenance, and had limited reliability
options.B: They used transistors and magnetic-core memory
options.C: They used integrated circuits and time-sharing
options.D: They used microprocessors and graphical user interfaces

questions.explanation: First-generation computers used vacuum tubes, magnetic drums or other early storage, punched cards and paper tape; they were relatively slow by modern standards, required substantial space and maintenance, and had limited reliability.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the second generation of computers?

options.A: They used vacuum tubes and punched cards
options.B: They were generally smaller, faster, more reliable and more energy-efficient than first-generation systems, and used magnetic-core memory and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL
options.C: They used integrated circuits and multiprogramming

questions.explanation: Second-generation computers were generally smaller, faster, more reliable and more energy-efficient than first-generation systems, and they used magnetic-core memory and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the third generation of computers?

options.A: They used vacuum tubes and were large and costly
options.B: They were smaller, faster, more reliable and less expensive to operate than earlier generations; operating systems, multiprogramming and time-sharing became more developed
options.C: They used microprocessors and graphical user interfaces
options.D: They used artificial intelligence and parallel processing

questions.explanation: Third-generation computers were smaller, faster, more reliable and less expensive to operate than earlier generations; operating systems, multiprogramming and time-sharing became more developed.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the fourth generation of computers?

options.A: They used vacuum tubes and machine language
options.B: Microprocessors enabled personal computers and smaller systems; processing power and storage capacity increased while cost and physical size generally decreased; graphical user interfaces and networking became widespread
options.C: They used integrated circuits and multiprogramming only
options.D: They used artificial intelligence and natural-language processing

questions.explanation: Microprocessors enabled personal computers and smaller systems; processing power and storage capacity increased while cost and physical size generally decreased. Graphical user interfaces and networking also became widespread during this broad era.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the fifth generation of computers?

options.A: It is commonly associated with artificial intelligence, knowledge-based systems, natural-language processing, parallel processing and advanced semiconductor technologies, and is not defined by one universally agreed hardware boundary
options.B: It is defined by the use of vacuum tubes
options.C: It is defined by the use of transistors
options.D: It is defined by the use of integrated circuits only

questions.explanation: Fifth-generation computing is commonly associated with artificial intelligence, knowledge-based systems, natural-language processing, parallel processing and advanced semiconductor technologies. It is not defined by one universally agreed hardware boundary.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the main difference between vacuum tubes and transistors?

options.A: Transistors are larger and generate more heat than vacuum tubes
options.B: Transistors are smaller, more energy-efficient, more reliable and generate less heat than the vacuum tubes they replaced
options.C: Vacuum tubes are more reliable than transistors
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Transistors are smaller, more energy-efficient, more reliable and generate less heat than the vacuum tubes they replaced in computer circuitry.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes an integrated circuit (IC)?

options.A: A vacuum tube used in first-generation computers
options.B: An electronic circuit in which multiple components such as transistors and resistors are fabricated together on a semiconductor chip
options.C: A type of secondary storage device

questions.explanation: An integrated circuit (IC) is an electronic circuit in which multiple components, such as transistors and resistors, are fabricated together on a semiconductor chip.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes what SSI, MSI, LSI, VLSI and ULSI mean?

options.A: Different types of secondary storage
options.B: Increasing levels of integration on semiconductor chips
options.C: Different generations of programming languages

questions.explanation: They describe increasing levels of integration on semiconductor chips: Small-Scale Integration, Medium-Scale Integration, Large-Scale Integration, Very-Large-Scale Integration and Ultra-Large-Scale Integration. Exact transistor-count boundaries can vary between references.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the usual order of computer generations and their key technologies?

options.A: First - transistors; second - vacuum tubes; third - microprocessors; fourth - integrated circuits; fifth - AI
options.B: First - vacuum tubes; second - transistors; third - integrated circuits; fourth - microprocessors/VLSI; fifth - AI-oriented and advanced computing technologies
options.C: First - integrated circuits; second - vacuum tubes; third - transistors; fourth - AI; fifth - microprocessors
options.D: First - microprocessors; second - integrated circuits; third - transistors; fourth - vacuum tubes; fifth - AI

questions.explanation: First generation - vacuum tubes; second generation - transistors; third generation - integrated circuits; fourth generation - microprocessors/VLSI; fifth generation - AI-oriented and advanced computing technologies.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the goals associated with fifth-generation computers?

options.A: Only faster arithmetic calculations
options.B: AI-oriented capabilities such as learning, reasoning, language processing, pattern recognition and solving complex problems
options.C: Only larger storage capacity

questions.explanation: The commonly stated goals include AI-oriented capabilities such as learning, reasoning, language processing, pattern recognition and solving complex problems. These are goals and research directions, not a single completed generation used uniformly in all classifications.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about generation dates and example classifications is correct?

options.A: They are exact and universally agreed upon
options.B: They are approximate; different textbooks may use slightly different cut-offs
options.C: They are defined only by the Indian government
options.D: They are based solely on software versions

questions.explanation: Generation dates and example classifications are approximate; different textbooks may use slightly different cut-offs.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about traditional size-based categories is correct?

options.A: They are useful for competitive-exam revision, but modern computing does not have strict boundaries between them
options.B: They are strictly defined and never overlap
options.C: They are based on software only
options.D: They are no longer used in any textbook

questions.explanation: The traditional size-based categories (micro, mini, mainframe and supercomputer) are useful for competitive-exam revision, but modern computing does not have strict boundaries between them.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about storage units is correct?

options.A: Decimal KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,024, while binary KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,000
options.B: Decimal KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,000, while binary KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,024
options.C: Both decimal and binary units use powers of 1,000
options.D: Both decimal and binary units use powers of 1,024

questions.explanation: Do not confuse storage units: decimal KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,000, while binary KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,024.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the fifth generation is correct?

options.A: It is a textbook classification associated with AI and advanced computing; there is no single universally accepted date range or definitive boundary
options.B: It has a universally accepted date range of 1980-1990
options.C: It is defined only by the use of vacuum tubes
options.D: It is defined only by the use of transistors

questions.explanation: The fifth generation is a textbook classification associated with AI and advanced computing; there is no single universally accepted date range or definitive boundary.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a computer function with its description?

options.A: Input - presenting results to the user
options.B: Process - entering data into the computer
options.C: Output - presenting processed information to the user

questions.explanation: In the IPO cycle, output is the presentation of processed information. Input is entering data, process is manipulating data according to instructions, and storage holds data and results.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can perform the same operation repeatedly and produce the same result under unchanged conditions?

options.A: Speed
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Consistency

questions.explanation: Consistency means a computer can perform the same operation repeatedly and produce the same result when the inputs, instructions and operating conditions are unchanged.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired?

options.A: Diligence
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Storage capacity

questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired or losing concentration in the human sense.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can carry out specified operations automatically with limited human intervention once programmed?

options.A: Versatility
options.B: Automation
options.C: Reliability

questions.explanation: Automation means that, once a program and required data are supplied, a computer can carry out the specified operations automatically with limited human intervention.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can be used for many different kinds of tasks?

options.A: Speed
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Versatility

questions.explanation: Versatility means a computer can be used for many different kinds of tasks, such as calculation, communication, design, record keeping and scientific analysis.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can operate dependably and produce expected results over time when properly maintained?

options.A: Reliability
options.B: Diligence
options.C: Versatility

questions.explanation: Reliability is the ability of a computer system to operate dependably and produce expected results over time when properly maintained.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between hardware and software?

options.A: Hardware is the collection of programs; software is the physical components
options.B: Hardware refers to physical components, while software is the collection of programs and instructions that direct the hardware
options.C: Hardware and software are both physical components
options.D: Hardware and software are both collections of programs

questions.explanation: Hardware refers to the physical, tangible components of a computer, while software is the collection of programs and related instructions that direct computer hardware to perform tasks.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is stored in non-volatile memory and provides low-level control for a device?

options.A: Application software
options.B: Firmware
options.C: RAM

questions.explanation: Firmware is software stored in non-volatile memory, usually in a device, that provides low-level control for that device.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions?

options.A: Mainframe computer
options.B: Supercomputer
options.C: Embedded computer

questions.explanation: An embedded computer is a computing system built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions, such as in vehicles, appliances, medical equipment and industrial machines.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is a complete computer built on one circuit board with processor, memory and input/output interfaces?

options.A: Single-board computer
options.B: Mainframe computer
options.C: Supercomputer

questions.explanation: A single-board computer is a complete computer built on one circuit board, with processor, memory and input/output interfaces; it is often used for education, prototyping and embedded projects.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is designed or configured to perform a specific task or a limited set of tasks?

options.A: General-purpose computer
options.B: Special-purpose computer
options.C: Mainframe computer

questions.explanation: A special-purpose computer is designed or configured to perform a specific task or a limited set of tasks, such as controlling a traffic signal or operating a dedicated industrial system.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is a high-performance computer intended for professional technical tasks such as engineering design and 3D graphics?

options.A: Desktop computer
options.B: Laptop computer
options.C: Workstation

questions.explanation: A workstation is a high-performance computer intended for professional technical tasks such as engineering design, scientific work, 3D graphics and specialised data processing.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is designed to be worn on the body, such as a smartwatch?

options.A: Mobile computer
options.B: Wearable computer
options.C: Embedded computer

questions.explanation: A wearable computer is a computing device designed to be worn on the body, such as a smartwatch or certain health-monitoring devices.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is a portable computing device designed to be used while being carried or moved?

options.A: Desktop computer
options.B: Mobile computer
options.C: Mainframe computer

questions.explanation: A mobile computer is a portable computing device, such as a laptop, tablet or smartphone, designed to be used while being carried or moved.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the units of storage in increasing order of size?

options.A: Bit, byte, kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, terabyte, petabyte
options.B: Byte, bit, kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, terabyte, petabyte
options.C: Bit, byte, megabyte, kilobyte, gigabyte, terabyte, petabyte
options.D: Kilobyte, bit, byte, megabyte, gigabyte, terabyte, petabyte

questions.explanation: Common units are bit, byte, kilobyte (KB), megabyte (MB), gigabyte (GB), terabyte (TB) and petabyte (PB).
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the contents of a CPU?

options.A: ALU, control unit and registers
options.B: RAM, ROM and cache
options.C: Hard disk, SSD and optical disc

questions.explanation: The CPU mainly contains the arithmetic logic unit (ALU), control unit (CU) and registers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which unit of a computer is directly accessible by the CPU and includes RAM and ROM?

options.A: Secondary storage
options.B: Primary memory
options.C: Output unit

questions.explanation: Primary memory is directly accessible by the CPU and includes RAM and ROM.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between a bit and a byte?

options.A: A byte is a single binary digit; a bit is a group of 8 bytes
options.B: A bit is a single binary digit; a byte is a group of 8 bits
options.C: A bit and a byte are the same unit
options.D: A byte is a group of 4 bits

questions.explanation: A bit (binary digit) is the smallest unit of digital data and can have one of two values: 0 or 1. A byte is a group of 8 bits.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which process loads the operating system into memory so that the system becomes ready for use?

options.A: Formatting
options.B: Booting
options.C: Defragmentation

questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting or restarting a computer and loading the operating system into memory so that the system becomes ready for use.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes cold booting from warm booting?

options.A: Cold booting restarts without switching off power; warm booting starts from a powered-off state
options.B: Cold booting starts from a powered-off state; warm booting restarts without completely switching off power
options.C: Cold booting and warm booting are identical processes
options.D: Cold booting is performed only through a restart command

questions.explanation: Cold booting starts a computer from a powered-off state; warm booting restarts a computer without completely switching off its power, usually through a restart command.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which generation of computers used machine language and vacuum tubes?

options.A: First generation
options.B: Second generation
options.C: Third generation

questions.explanation: First-generation computers used vacuum tubes for circuitry and often used machine language.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which generation of computers used magnetic-core memory and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL?

options.A: First generation
options.B: Second generation
options.C: Third generation

questions.explanation: Second-generation computers used magnetic-core memory and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: During which generation did operating systems, multiprogramming and time-sharing become more developed?

options.A: First generation
options.B: Second generation
options.C: Third generation

questions.explanation: In the third generation, operating systems, multiprogramming and time-sharing became more developed.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: During which generation did graphical user interfaces and networking become widespread?

options.A: First generation
options.B: Second generation
options.C: Third generation

questions.explanation: Graphical user interfaces and networking became widespread during the fourth generation.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a commonly cited first-generation computer?

options.A: ENIAC
options.B: EDVAC
options.C: IBM 1401

questions.explanation: IBM 1401 is a commonly cited second-generation computer, while ENIAC, EDVAC, EDSAC and UNIVAC I are first-generation computers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a commonly cited second-generation computer?

options.A: IBM 1401
options.B: IBM 7090
options.C: IBM 7094

questions.explanation: IBM System/360 is a commonly cited third-generation computer, while IBM 1401 and IBM 7090/7094 are second-generation computers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a computer generation with its key technology?

options.A: First generation - transistors
options.B: Second generation - vacuum tubes
options.C: Third generation - integrated circuits

questions.explanation: Third generation - integrated circuits. First generation used vacuum tubes, second generation used transistors, and fourth generation used microprocessors/VLSI.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a commonly cited example of a fourth-generation computer?

options.A: ENIAC
options.B: IBM 1401
options.C: IBM System/360

questions.explanation: IBM PC-compatible personal computers and Apple Macintosh systems are commonly cited examples of the microprocessor era (fourth generation).
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: Speed
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Emotions

questions.explanation: A computer has no inherent human judgement or emotions. Speed, accuracy and diligence are characteristics of a computer.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main limitation of a computer?

options.A: It depends on correct instructions and suitable input
options.B: It has inherent human judgement and emotions
options.C: It requires electricity or power
options.D: It may be affected by hardware failure, software defects, cyberattacks and data loss

questions.explanation: A computer has no inherent human judgement or emotions. The other options are limitations of a computer.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in e-governance?

options.A: Using information and communication technology to improve government administration and public service delivery, such as online certificates, applications, payments and status tracking
options.B: Using computers only for defence and security
options.C: Using computers only for private business accounting

questions.explanation: E-governance uses information and communication technology to improve government administration and public service delivery, such as online certificates, applications, payments and status tracking.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in weather forecasting?

options.A: They control the weather directly
options.B: They process observations and run numerical models to estimate future atmospheric conditions
options.C: They only record past weather data
options.D: They eliminate the need for observations

questions.explanation: They process observations and run numerical models to estimate future atmospheric conditions; forecasts depend on the quality of data and models.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in libraries?

options.A: Only for issuing books
options.B: For cataloguing, digital libraries, circulation records, search systems, membership management and access to electronic resources
options.C: Only for membership management

questions.explanation: They support cataloguing, digital libraries, circulation records, search systems, membership management and access to electronic resources.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a microcomputer and a mainframe?

options.A: A microcomputer is based on a microprocessor and designed primarily for individual use, while a mainframe is a powerful, highly reliable system for large volumes of transactions, data and concurrent users
options.B: A microcomputer is designed for large-scale transaction processing, while a mainframe is designed for individual use
options.C: A microcomputer and a mainframe are the same type of computer
options.D: A microcomputer is always larger than a mainframe

questions.explanation: A microcomputer is a computer based on a microprocessor and designed primarily for individual use. A mainframe is a powerful, highly reliable system designed to handle large volumes of transactions, data and concurrent users.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a supercomputer and a mainframe?

options.A: A supercomputer is optimised for high-volume transaction processing, while a mainframe is optimised for complex numerical problems
options.B: A supercomputer is optimised for extremely fast computation on complex numerical problems, while a mainframe is optimised for high-volume input/output, transaction processing, reliability and many concurrent users
options.C: Both are optimised for the same type of workload
options.D: A mainframe is always faster than a supercomputer

questions.explanation: A supercomputer is optimised for extremely fast computation on complex numerical problems, often using parallel processing; a mainframe is optimised for high-volume input/output, transaction processing, reliability and support for many concurrent users.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a server and a mainframe?

options.A: A server is defined by the role of providing network services and can range from a small machine to a large system; a mainframe is a class of enterprise computer designed for high-volume, reliable processing, and a mainframe can also perform server roles
options.B: A server is always larger than a mainframe
options.C: A mainframe cannot provide network services
options.D: A server is a class of enterprise computer; a mainframe is defined only by network role

questions.explanation: A server is defined by the role of providing network services and can range from a small machine to a large system; a mainframe is a class of enterprise computer designed for high-volume, reliable processing. A mainframe can also perform server roles.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the IPO cycle along with the additional essential function?

options.A: Input-Process-Output, with storage also being an essential computer function
options.B: Input-Program-Output, with networking also being an essential computer function
options.C: Information-Process-Organisation, with printing also being an essential computer function
options.D: Input-Processing-Organisation, with scanning also being an essential computer function

questions.explanation: The IPO cycle means Input-Process-Output: data are entered, processed according to instructions, and presented as information. Storage is also an essential computer function.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of registers in a CPU?

options.A: They provide long-term persistent storage of data
options.B: They are very small, very fast storage locations inside the CPU that temporarily hold data, instructions, addresses or intermediate results during processing
options.C: They perform arithmetic and logical operations
options.D: They control the flow of instructions between the CPU and memory

questions.explanation: Registers are very small, very fast storage locations inside the CPU that temporarily hold data, instructions, addresses or intermediate results during processing.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the Control Unit (CU)?

options.A: It performs arithmetic operations such as addition and subtraction
options.B: It stores data permanently without power
options.C: It directs and coordinates computer operations by controlling the flow of instructions and data between the CPU, memory and input/output devices
options.D: It displays output to the user

questions.explanation: The control unit directs and coordinates computer operations by controlling the flow of instructions and data between the CPU, memory and input/output devices.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the ALU?

options.A: It performs arithmetic operations such as addition and subtraction and logical/comparison operations such as AND, OR, NOT, less-than and equality
options.B: It controls the flow of instructions between the CPU and memory
options.C: It stores data permanently without power
options.D: It displays output to the user

questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic operations such as addition and subtraction and logical/comparison operations such as AND, OR, NOT, less-than and equality.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the CPU?

options.A: It stores data permanently without power
options.B: It fetches, decodes and executes instructions and coordinates system operations
options.C: It displays output to the user
options.D: It provides long-term persistent storage of data

questions.explanation: The CPU is the principal processing unit of a computer. It fetches, decodes and executes instructions and coordinates system operations; it includes the control unit, ALU and registers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between primary memory and secondary storage?

options.A: Primary memory is directly accessible by the CPU and generally faster; secondary storage stores data persistently and usually has greater capacity
options.B: Primary memory is slower and has greater capacity than secondary storage
options.C: Secondary storage is directly accessible by the CPU; primary memory is not
options.D: Primary memory is non-volatile; secondary storage is volatile

questions.explanation: Primary memory is directly accessible by the CPU and is generally faster; it includes RAM and ROM. Secondary storage, such as an SSD, hard disk or optical disc, stores data persistently and usually has greater capacity.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between volatile and non-volatile memory?

options.A: Volatile memory retains contents without power; non-volatile memory requires power
options.B: Volatile memory requires power to retain its contents; non-volatile memory retains data without power
options.C: Both volatile and non-volatile memory require power to retain contents
options.D: Both volatile and non-volatile memory lose contents when power is switched off

questions.explanation: Volatile memory requires power to retain its contents, as with ordinary RAM; non-volatile memory retains data without power, as with ROM, flash memory and SSD storage.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes GIGO?

options.A: Accurate input always produces accurate output
options.B: Inaccurate, incomplete or unsuitable input can lead to inaccurate or unsuitable output, even when the computer processes it correctly
options.C: The computer corrects all errors in input automatically
options.D: Output quality is independent of input quality

questions.explanation: GIGO stands for Garbage In, Garbage Out. It means that inaccurate, incomplete or unsuitable input can lead to inaccurate or unsuitable output, even when the computer processes it correctly.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a program?

options.A: A physical component of a computer
options.B: A set of instructions written in a programming language that tells a computer what operations to perform
options.C: Raw data stored in memory
options.D: The output produced by a computer

questions.explanation: A program is a set of instructions written in a programming language that tells a computer what operations to perform.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes firmware?

options.A: Application software used for word processing
options.B: Software stored in non-volatile memory, usually in a device, that provides low-level control for that device
options.C: Volatile memory that loses contents when power is off
options.D: The physical components of a computer

questions.explanation: Firmware is software stored in non-volatile memory, usually in a device, that provides low-level control for that device; examples include firmware in routers and embedded controllers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes system software from application software?

options.A: System software performs user-oriented tasks; application software manages hardware
options.B: System software manages computer hardware and provides a platform for applications; application software performs user-oriented tasks
options.C: System software includes word processors; application software includes operating systems
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: System software manages computer hardware and provides a platform for applications; examples include operating systems and device drivers. Application software performs user-oriented tasks; examples include word processors, spreadsheets and web browsers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes data?

options.A: Processed and organised information
options.B: Raw facts, figures, symbols or observations that have not yet been organised or interpreted
options.C: A set of instructions written in a programming language

questions.explanation: Data are raw facts, figures, symbols or observations that have not yet been organised or interpreted; examples include 25, 'Ravi' and 12-06-2026.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes information?

options.A: Raw facts and figures
options.B: A collection of programs
options.C: Processed, organised or interpreted data that has meaning and is useful to a user
options.D: The physical parts of a computer

questions.explanation: Information is processed, organised or interpreted data that has meaning and is useful to a user; for example, a report showing the total marks obtained by a student.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between data and information?

options.A: Data are processed; information is raw
options.B: Data are raw and unprocessed facts, whereas information is data processed into a meaningful and useful form
options.C: Data are stored; information is not stored
options.D: There is no difference between data and information

questions.explanation: Data are raw and unprocessed facts, whereas information is data processed into a meaningful and useful form.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the basic functional units of a computer?

options.A: Input unit, memory/storage unit, CPU and output unit
options.B: Keyboard, mouse, monitor and printer
options.C: RAM, ROM, hard disk and pen drive
options.D: Operating system, application software, firmware and hardware

questions.explanation: The basic functional units are the input unit, memory/storage unit, central processing unit (CPU) and output unit. The CPU mainly contains the ALU, control unit and registers.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a bit?

options.A: A group of 8 bytes
options.B: The smallest unit of digital data that can have one of two values: 0 or 1
options.C: A unit of storage equal to 1,000 bytes

questions.explanation: A bit (binary digit) is the smallest unit of digital data and can have one of two values: 0 or 1.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a byte?

options.A: A single binary digit
options.B: A group of 8 bits, commonly used as a basic unit for representing a character or measuring storage
options.C: A unit of processing speed

questions.explanation: A byte is a group of 8 bits. It is commonly used as a basic unit for representing a character or measuring storage.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: In decimal storage measurement, which of the following is correct?

options.A: 1 KB = 1,024 bytes
options.B: 1 KB = 1,000 bytes
options.C: 1 KB = 100 bytes

questions.explanation: In decimal storage measurement, 1 KB = 1,000 bytes.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes binary units of storage?

options.A: KiB, MiB, GiB and TiB, each based on 1,024
options.B: KB, MB, GB and TB, each based on 1,000
options.C: Bit, byte, nibble and word

questions.explanation: Binary units use KiB, MiB, GiB and TiB, each based on 1,024.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes booting?

options.A: The process of starting or restarting a computer and loading the operating system into memory so that the system becomes ready for use
options.B: The process of installing application software
options.C: The process of deleting files from the hard disk
options.D: The process of connecting a computer to a network

questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting or restarting a computer and loading the operating system into memory so that the system becomes ready for use.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes speed as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.B: The ability to perform very large numbers of operations in a short time
options.C: The ability to repeat tasks without getting tired
options.D: The ability to use many different kinds of tasks

questions.explanation: A computer can perform very large numbers of operations in a short time. Processing speed is commonly expressed using units such as hertz (Hz) and its multiples.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes accuracy as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to perform very large numbers of operations in a short time
options.B: The ability to produce highly accurate results when the input data, instructions and hardware are correct
options.C: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.D: The ability to repeat tasks without getting tired

questions.explanation: A computer can produce highly accurate results when the input data, instructions and hardware are correct; incorrect input or instructions can produce incorrect output.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes diligence as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to produce accurate results
options.B: The ability to repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired or losing concentration in the human sense
options.C: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.D: The ability to perform many different kinds of tasks

questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired or losing concentration in the human sense.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes storage capacity as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to perform very large numbers of operations in a short time
options.B: The ability to store large quantities of data and retrieve them when required
options.C: The ability to repeat tasks without getting tired
options.D: The ability to produce the same result repeatedly

questions.explanation: A computer can store large quantities of data and retrieve them when required, using primary memory and secondary storage devices.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes automation as a characteristic of a computer?

options.A: The ability to store large quantities of data
options.B: The ability to carry out specified operations automatically with limited human intervention once a program and required data are supplied
options.C: The ability to perform many different kinds of tasks
options.D: The ability to produce accurate results

questions.explanation: Automation means that, once a program and required data are supplied, a computer can carry out the specified operations automatically with limited human intervention.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes multitasking?

options.A: The ability of a computer to store large quantities of data
options.B: The operating system's ability to manage more than one task or program during the same period by sharing processor time and other resources
options.C: The ability of a computer to perform calculations automatically
options.D: The ability of a computer to produce the same result repeatedly

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the operating system's ability to manage more than one task or program during the same period, by sharing processor time and other resources.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in banking and finance?

options.A: Only for printing passbooks
options.B: For account management, electronic fund transfers, ATM services, online banking, transaction processing, financial analysis, accounting and fraud monitoring
options.C: Only for customer relationship management

questions.explanation: Computers support account management, electronic fund transfers, ATM services, online banking, transaction processing, financial analysis, accounting and fraud monitoring.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in industry and manufacturing?

options.A: Only for production planning
options.B: For automation, robotics, computer-aided design (CAD), computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), quality control, process monitoring and production planning
options.C: Only for quality control

questions.explanation: They support automation, robotics, computer-aided design (CAD), computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), quality control, process monitoring and production planning.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in defence and security?

options.A: Only for communication
options.B: For communication, surveillance systems, training simulations, logistics, intelligence analysis, navigation and command-and-control systems, subject to strict security controls
options.C: Only for training simulations

questions.explanation: They support communication, surveillance systems, training simulations, logistics, intelligence analysis, navigation and command-and-control systems, subject to strict security controls.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in agriculture?

options.A: Only for weather information
options.B: For weather and market information, precision farming, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation control, farm management and analysis of satellite or sensor data
options.C: Only for irrigation control

questions.explanation: They support weather and market information, precision farming, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation control, farm management and analysis of satellite or sensor data.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in entertainment and media?

options.A: Only for gaming
options.B: For gaming, animation, video and audio editing, digital photography, streaming, publishing and special effects
options.C: Only for video and audio editing

questions.explanation: They are used for gaming, animation, video and audio editing, digital photography, streaming, publishing and special effects.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in transportation?

options.A: Only for ticket reservations
options.B: For ticket reservations, traffic management, navigation, vehicle control systems, logistics, scheduling and tracking of goods
options.C: Only for navigation

questions.explanation: They support ticket reservations, traffic management, navigation, vehicle control systems, logistics, scheduling and tracking of goods.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the use of computers in communication?

options.A: Only for email
options.B: For email, instant messaging, video conferencing, internet-based voice calls, social networking and sharing of digital files
options.C: Only for video conferencing

questions.explanation: They enable email, instant messaging, video conferencing, internet-based voice calls, social networking and sharing of digital files.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Applications of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
