options.B: They were generally smaller, faster, more reliable and more energy-efficient than first-generation systems, and used magnetic-core memory and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL
options.C: They used integrated circuits and multiprogramming

questions.explanation: Second-generation computers were generally smaller, faster, more reliable and more energy-efficient than first-generation systems, and they used magnetic-core memory and high-level languages such as FORTRAN and COBOL.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the third generation of computers?

options.A: They used vacuum tubes and were large and costly
options.B: They were smaller, faster, more reliable and less expensive to operate than earlier generations; operating systems, multiprogramming and time-sharing became more developed
options.C: They used microprocessors and graphical user interfaces
options.D: They used artificial intelligence and parallel processing

questions.explanation: Third-generation computers were smaller, faster, more reliable and less expensive to operate than earlier generations; operating systems, multiprogramming and time-sharing became more developed.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the fourth generation of computers?

options.A: They used vacuum tubes and machine language
options.B: Microprocessors enabled personal computers and smaller systems; processing power and storage capacity increased while cost and physical size generally decreased; graphical user interfaces and networking became widespread
options.C: They used integrated circuits and multiprogramming only
options.D: They used artificial intelligence and natural-language processing

questions.explanation: Microprocessors enabled personal computers and smaller systems; processing power and storage capacity increased while cost and physical size generally decreased. Graphical user interfaces and networking also became widespread during this broad era.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the fifth generation of computers?

options.A: It is commonly associated with artificial intelligence, knowledge-based systems, natural-language processing, parallel processing and advanced semiconductor technologies, and is not defined by one universally agreed hardware boundary
options.B: It is defined by the use of vacuum tubes
options.C: It is defined by the use of transistors
options.D: It is defined by the use of integrated circuits only

questions.explanation: Fifth-generation computing is commonly associated with artificial intelligence, knowledge-based systems, natural-language processing, parallel processing and advanced semiconductor technologies. It is not defined by one universally agreed hardware boundary.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the main difference between vacuum tubes and transistors?

options.A: Transistors are larger and generate more heat than vacuum tubes
options.B: Transistors are smaller, more energy-efficient, more reliable and generate less heat than the vacuum tubes they replaced
options.C: Vacuum tubes are more reliable than transistors
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Transistors are smaller, more energy-efficient, more reliable and generate less heat than the vacuum tubes they replaced in computer circuitry.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes an integrated circuit (IC)?

options.A: A vacuum tube used in first-generation computers
options.B: An electronic circuit in which multiple components such as transistors and resistors are fabricated together on a semiconductor chip
options.C: A type of secondary storage device

questions.explanation: An integrated circuit (IC) is an electronic circuit in which multiple components, such as transistors and resistors, are fabricated together on a semiconductor chip.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes what SSI, MSI, LSI, VLSI and ULSI mean?

options.A: Different types of secondary storage
options.B: Increasing levels of integration on semiconductor chips
options.C: Different generations of programming languages

questions.explanation: They describe increasing levels of integration on semiconductor chips: Small-Scale Integration, Medium-Scale Integration, Large-Scale Integration, Very-Large-Scale Integration and Ultra-Large-Scale Integration. Exact transistor-count boundaries can vary between references.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the usual order of computer generations and their key technologies?

options.A: First - transistors; second - vacuum tubes; third - microprocessors; fourth - integrated circuits; fifth - AI
options.B: First - vacuum tubes; second - transistors; third - integrated circuits; fourth - microprocessors/VLSI; fifth - AI-oriented and advanced computing technologies
options.C: First - integrated circuits; second - vacuum tubes; third - transistors; fourth - AI; fifth - microprocessors
options.D: First - microprocessors; second - integrated circuits; third - transistors; fourth - vacuum tubes; fifth - AI

questions.explanation: First generation - vacuum tubes; second generation - transistors; third generation - integrated circuits; fourth generation - microprocessors/VLSI; fifth generation - AI-oriented and advanced computing technologies.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the goals associated with fifth-generation computers?

options.A: Only faster arithmetic calculations
options.B: AI-oriented capabilities such as learning, reasoning, language processing, pattern recognition and solving complex problems
options.C: Only larger storage capacity

questions.explanation: The commonly stated goals include AI-oriented capabilities such as learning, reasoning, language processing, pattern recognition and solving complex problems. These are goals and research directions, not a single completed generation used uniformly in all classifications.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Generations of computers

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about generation dates and example classifications is correct?

options.A: They are exact and universally agreed upon
options.B: They are approximate; different textbooks may use slightly different cut-offs
options.C: They are defined only by the Indian government
options.D: They are based solely on software versions

questions.explanation: Generation dates and example classifications are approximate; different textbooks may use slightly different cut-offs.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about traditional size-based categories is correct?

options.A: They are useful for competitive-exam revision, but modern computing does not have strict boundaries between them
options.B: They are strictly defined and never overlap
options.C: They are based on software only
options.D: They are no longer used in any textbook

questions.explanation: The traditional size-based categories (micro, mini, mainframe and supercomputer) are useful for competitive-exam revision, but modern computing does not have strict boundaries between them.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about storage units is correct?

options.A: Decimal KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,024, while binary KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,000
options.B: Decimal KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,000, while binary KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,024
options.C: Both decimal and binary units use powers of 1,000
options.D: Both decimal and binary units use powers of 1,024

questions.explanation: Do not confuse storage units: decimal KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,000, while binary KB/MB/GB use powers of 1,024.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the fifth generation is correct?

options.A: It is a textbook classification associated with AI and advanced computing; there is no single universally accepted date range or definitive boundary
options.B: It has a universally accepted date range of 1980-1990
options.C: It is defined only by the use of vacuum tubes
options.D: It is defined only by the use of transistors

questions.explanation: The fifth generation is a textbook classification associated with AI and advanced computing; there is no single universally accepted date range or definitive boundary.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Exam accuracy notes

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a computer function with its description?

options.A: Input - presenting results to the user
options.B: Process - entering data into the computer
options.C: Output - presenting processed information to the user

questions.explanation: In the IPO cycle, output is the presentation of processed information. Input is entering data, process is manipulating data according to instructions, and storage holds data and results.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can perform the same operation repeatedly and produce the same result under unchanged conditions?

options.A: Speed
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Consistency

questions.explanation: Consistency means a computer can perform the same operation repeatedly and produce the same result when the inputs, instructions and operating conditions are unchanged.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired?

options.A: Diligence
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Storage capacity

questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can repeat tasks for long periods without getting tired or losing concentration in the human sense.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can carry out specified operations automatically with limited human intervention once programmed?

options.A: Versatility
options.B: Automation
options.C: Reliability

questions.explanation: Automation means that, once a program and required data are supplied, a computer can carry out the specified operations automatically with limited human intervention.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can be used for many different kinds of tasks?

options.A: Speed
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Versatility

questions.explanation: Versatility means a computer can be used for many different kinds of tasks, such as calculation, communication, design, record keeping and scientific analysis.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer means it can operate dependably and produce expected results over time when properly maintained?

options.A: Reliability
options.B: Diligence
options.C: Versatility

questions.explanation: Reliability is the ability of a computer system to operate dependably and produce expected results over time when properly maintained.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Characteristics and limitations

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between hardware and software?

options.A: Hardware is the collection of programs; software is the physical components
options.B: Hardware refers to physical components, while software is the collection of programs and instructions that direct the hardware
options.C: Hardware and software are both physical components
options.D: Hardware and software are both collections of programs

questions.explanation: Hardware refers to the physical, tangible components of a computer, while software is the collection of programs and related instructions that direct computer hardware to perform tasks.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is stored in non-volatile memory and provides low-level control for a device?

options.A: Application software
options.B: Firmware
options.C: RAM

questions.explanation: Firmware is software stored in non-volatile memory, usually in a device, that provides low-level control for that device.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Definition and basic concepts

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of computer is built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions?

options.A: Mainframe computer
options.B: Supercomputer
options.C: Embedded computer

questions.explanation: An embedded computer is a computing system built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions, such as in vehicles, appliances, medical equipment and industrial machines.
questions.source: 18.1 Computer Fundamentals - Types and classification of computers
